html:
The Lumbee are a Native American people centred in Robeson County, North Carolina, along the Lumber River; with about 55,000 enrolled members they are the largest tribe east of the Mississippi. They descend from several Southeastern peoples, especially Siouan, Iroquoian and Algonquian speakers of the Carolinas such as the Cheraw, who gathered in the swamps of the area in the 1700s, together with some people of European and African descent.

During and after the American Civil War, Henry Berry Lowry led a band that fought Confederate home guards and local officials for years. In 1958 Lumbee men broke up a Ku Klux Klan rally at Hayes Pond, an event still celebrated. The Lumbee Act of 1956 recognised their name but withheld federal benefits, starting a long campaign for full recognition. Nearby peoples include the Coharie and the Tuscarora.
